manifest.scope: local Web, CLI, HTTP, MCP and SDKs; full R0-R7 acceptance not complete

review_fixes: Audio-only native decode verification now uses an audio stream instead of requiring a video stream.
Caption proposal validates once and commits one ordinary reversible journal transaction without relaxing the frozen 128-operation edit limit.
Typed public transcription projection rejects corrupted result/input locks even if both were forged together.
Non-UUID and safely encoded project identifiers support direct GET/HEAD reloads; decoding never chooses a filesystem path.
Guide popover uses a bounded portal to avoid clipping by resizable panels; outside/Esc closes and reduced-motion entrance remain scoped.
Viewport geometry and transform handles share actual canvas coordinates; floating fit residue is removed and panning is bounded.
Browser verification waits for the HttpOnly session bootstrap and resets only its named synthetic project through shared edits so repeated runs do not overlap older captions.
Three remaining editor Chinese labels corrected after screenshot review.
limits: The 9 caption-browser groups include four viewport groups also present in the 45-flow regression; do not add them as unique coverage.
Real small-model recognition was accepted for one synthesized English sentence, not all nine selectable languages or noisy recordings.
Caption chunks estimate word timing inside speech segments; current CaptionCue output does not replace Classic independent text elements/typography.
The host model is external, pinned by hash and configured outside Web; the development archive does not bundle a speech model.
Scene analysis currently admits all fixed scene dependencies; an audio-only dependency optimization is still open.
57 Classic groups currently include 16 specified-flow verified, 23 unmigrated, 14 partial, 3 pending equivalence and 1 Classic placeholder.
The package is a local x86_64 macOS development delivery, not complete R0-R7 release, cross-platform, Safari/Firefox or 4K performance acceptance.
Agent acceptance uses actual external editing tools with deterministic synthetic fixtures; autonomous editorial taste is not assessed.
